text: Writing clean code is about making your work easy for others—and your future self—to understand. The most important rule is readability: if someone can read your code like a simple story, you have succeeded. This starts with naming conventions. Variable names like `userAge` or `totalPrice` are clear, while names like `x` or `data1` are vague and confusing. Instead of writing one long block of logic, break it into small, focused functions that each do one job, like `calculateDiscount` or `validateEmail`. This makes your code easier to test and reuse. Finally, think about maintainability. When you return to a project after months, clean code helps you fix bugs and add features quickly. Investing time in clarity now saves hours of confusion later.
